title: acetosella minuta
intro: Acetosella minuta, commonly known as small cranberry or bog whortleberry, is a small, low-growing shrub native to peat bogs in northern Europe. This plant has been used for its medicinal properties, with reported health benefits including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects, which may help to soothe digestive issues and support immune function. The therapeutic actions of Acetosella minuta include antiseptic, antispasmodic, and vulnerary properties, making it useful for treating wounds, relieving cramps, and promoting healing. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to contribute to its medicinal properties.
